# WattBench 1.1 — implementation plan (generated by design workflow, 2026-09-25)

## Vision

WattBench 1.1 is the release that turns a working demo into an instrument you can trust on the bench: recordings survive a locked phone, a swipe-kill and a Bluetooth drop (append-only journal + bluetooth-central + state restoration, gaps drawn instead of hidden); the Live tab becomes a single Apple-style instrument face (status pill, one hero numeral with rolling digits, two secondary tiles with peak captions, one scrubbable chart, a Voice-Memos-style Record bar with markers and auto-stop); an always-on trip counter answers "how many mAh went into that" without naming a session; Sessions becomes a day-grouped, searchable, sparklined list whose detail screen is a report (stat tiles, per-metric scroll/zoom chart with min/max envelope, drag range selection with slice stats, markers, notes, ShareLink CSV); connection is zero-tap with honest backoff and give-up; a Settings form absorbs Diagnostics, demo, units and keep-awake; and threshold alerts with local notifications let the bench run itself. Everything analytic is pure Swift under Model/ with XCTest coverage, storage scales to hundreds of hour-long sessions, and every inferred number carries an "estimate" caption. Live Activity, event detection, charge-phase analysis, compare and landscape Bench Mode are queued behind it as 1.2.

## UI direction

NAVIGATION. Two tabs stay: Live (waveform.path.ecg) and Sessions (clock.arrow.circlepath). Live = NavigationStack, large title "WattBench" collapsing on scroll; topBarLeading = StatusPill (tap opens Connect sheet, .presentationDetents([.medium, .large])); topBarTrailing = one gear button opening SettingsView as a sheet (Diagnostics, Alerts, Demo, About live inside it as NavigationLinks). Body order, no scrolling needed on a 6.1-inch phone at default text size: HeroReadout, TripCard, MetricChartCard; RecordBar pinned with .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) on .bar material. Recording setup is a sheet at .medium detent, never an .alert with a TextField. Sessions = List(.insetGrouped) grouped by day, .searchable, detail pushed via NavigationPath(UUID). While recording, the Sessions tab shows a red dot + Text(timerInterval:) chip in topBarLeading that switches AppRouter.tab back to .live. Errors are inline (Label under the pill, banner via safeAreaInset(.top)); alerts only for destructive confirmations.
TYPE SCALE. Hero value: .system(size: 56, weight: .semibold, design: .rounded).monospacedDigit().minimumScaleFactor(0.5).lineLimit(1), unit .title3 .secondary in HStack(alignment: .lastTextBaseline). Secondary tiles and stat tiles: .system(.title2, design: .rounded).weight(.semibold).monospacedDigit(). Labels: .caption2.weight(.semibold).textCase(.uppercase).tracking(0.8).foregroundStyle(.secondary). Table values: .callout.monospacedDigit(). Every number that changes gets .monospacedDigit() and .contentTransition(.numericText(value: v)) + .animation(.snappy(duration: 0.25), value: v), both disabled when accessibilityReduceMotion. Elapsed time always via Text(timerInterval:countsDown: false) or Duration.formatted(.time(pattern: .hourMinuteSecond)); never a 1 Hz TimelineView. Numbers always come from MetricFormatter (auto-ranged mA/mW/mWh, hysteresis, locale decimal separator); never String(format:).
COLOR. Three semantic colorsets in Assets.xcassets: Voltage (light systemBlue, dark #5AC8FA), Current (light systemOrange, dark #FF9F0A), Power (light systemGreen, dark #30D158), exposed as Color.voltage/.current/.power and Metric.color. AccentColor (cyan) only for interactive chrome. Red only for Record/Stop, destructive actions and fired alerts; purple only for Demo. Comparison palettes (later) never reuse V/A/W hues. Dark mode is the primary bench appearance; every screen is checked in both.
MATERIAL AND SHAPE. Page background Color(.systemGroupedBackground); cards Color(.secondarySystemGroupedBackground) in .rect(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous) with 16pt inner padding, 16pt horizontal page gutter, 12pt between cards. Materials only for floating chrome: StatusPill (.thinMaterial capsule), RecordBar (.bar), chart scrub annotation (.regularMaterial, radius 8), alert banner (.thinMaterial). One FloatingChrome view modifier in Views/Components wraps these and applies .glassEffect() under if #available(iOS 26) so custom chrome matches system Liquid Glass when built with the iOS 26/27 SDK (machine has Xcode 27.0; deployment target stays 17.0). No custom tab bar or navigation bar backgrounds.
CHARTS. LineMark .interpolationMethod(.monotone), lineWidth 2, AreaMark LinearGradient(metric color 0.25 -> 0). Live chart uses chartScrollableAxes(.horizontal) + chartXVisibleDomain(length: window) + chartXSelection(value:) with a hairline RuleMark and material capsule readout; the chart line is never animated. Y domain .automatic(includesZero: false) padded 5 percent by Decimator.yDomain. Gaps > 5 s render as RectangleMark bands with .foregroundStyle(.secondary.opacity(0.15)). Markers are dashed RuleMarks with .annotation(position: .top) capsule labels in accent; peak-hold is a dashed RuleMark(y:) in the metric color at 0.6 opacity. Sessions detail adds a min/max envelope (AreaMark yStart/yEnd at 0.18 opacity) under the mean line when a bucket holds > 1 sample. Every value that is inferred or estimated carries a .caption2 "estimate" or "peak (100 ms)" caption.
MOTION AND HAPTICS. Springs only (.snappy). SF Symbol effects with meaning: antenna .variableColor.iterative while scanning/reconnecting, record.circle .pulse while recording, .bounce once on connect, .contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace)) when Record flips to Stop. Haptics through .sensoryFeedback keyed on model counters, never per sample: .success on connect, .warning on error/drop/alert, .start/.stop on record, .impact(weight: .light) on save/delete/trip reset, .selection on metric/window switch. All gated on accessibilityReduceMotion via FeedbackModifiers.
EMPTY AND ERROR STATES. ContentUnavailableView with a primary action everywhere: Live never-connected ("No Meter Connected", powermeter symbol, Connect + Try Demo Data); Connect sheet per state (Bluetooth off, unauthorized with Open Settings, scanning with ProgressView, nothing found after 8 s with meter-menu hint); Sessions empty and .search variants. Demo mode shows a persistent thin "Demo data, simulated readings" banner under the nav bar and a purple pill so App Review can never mistake it. Accessibility: readouts are single accessibility elements with spoken values from MetricFormatter.spoken, 44pt minimum targets, ViewThatFits for tile rows at accessibility sizes.

## Architecture

MODULE LAYOUT (single app target, folders become ownership boundaries): Bluetooth/ (MeterManager, FNB58Protocol) - CoreBluetooth only; Model/Pipeline/ (SamplePipeline, RingBuffer, ChartSnapshot, TripMeter, Extremes, SampleObserver, AutoStopRule) - pure Swift fed by every source; Model/Storage/ (SessionStore, SessionSummary, RecordingJournal, LegacyMigration) - Foundation only; Model/Analysis/ (Decimator, RangeStats, ThresholdMonitor, SessionQuery) - pure functions/value types; Model/Format/ (Metric, MetricFormatter, Preferences); Model/Reading.swift (Reading, SessionStats, Session, Marker); Views/Live, Views/Sessions, Views/Connect, Views/Settings, Views/Alerts, Views/Components; Export/ (SessionExport Transferable); Alerts/ (AlertCoordinator, AlertNotifier). Tests mirror folders under WattBenchTests/.
DATA FLOW. Source (CB notify callback or DemoSource timer or FixtureSource replay) -> FNB58Protocol.parse -> Reading(timestamp: Date(), monotonic: ContinuousClock seconds) -> MeterManager.ingest -> SamplePipeline.ingest(r): (1) latest = r, (2) RingBuffer<Reading>(capacity 1200).append, (3) extremes.update(r), (4) each TripMeter.add(r, dt), (5) recording?.add(r) which appends a 16-byte record to RecordingJournal and updates SessionStats and evaluates AutoStopRule, (6) observers.forEach { $0.observe(r, context) } (ThresholdMonitor/AlertCoordinator), (7) if now - lastChartPublish >= 0.2 s publish ChartSnapshot (windowed, decimated to <= 600 points, yDomain) so SwiftUI redraws the chart at <= 5 Hz while the hero numeral still updates at 10 Hz from `latest`. Auto-stop returns a reason -> MeterManager.stopRecording(reason:) -> SessionStore.save -> recordingEventCount += 1.
THREADING. MeterManager, SamplePipeline, SessionRecorder, SessionStore, AlertCoordinator, Preferences are all @MainActor (CB central stays on .main queue; annotate now so Swift 6 mode and the later widget/intent targets do not force a rewrite). RecordingJournal owns a serial DispatchQueue(label: "wattbench.journal", qos: .utility): ingest enqueues 16-byte records into an in-memory Data buffer on the main actor and the queue flushes with FileHandle.write + synchronize every 1 s or 64 records, whichever first. Journal reads, legacy migration, sample decoding for detail views and CSV writing run in Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) and hop back to the main actor with results. Demo Timer is foreground-only (documented); BLE notifications keep arriving in background with the bluetooth-central mode.
STORAGE. Documents/sessions/<uuid>/manifest.json (SessionSummary: id, schemaVersion 2, name, startTime, endTime, deviceName, stats, sampleCount, markers, tags, notes, autoStopReason, state recording|complete|recovered, sparkline [Float] 60 points) + samples.wbj (header 16 bytes: magic "WBJ1", UInt16 version = 1, UInt16 reserved, Float64 startEpoch; then records of UInt32 t_ms offset from startEpoch + Int32 V, I, W in native 1/10000 units, little endian, 16 bytes each; record count = (fileSize - 16) / 16, trailing partial record ignored). Legacy v1 <uuid>.json files are migrated on first launch (write folder, verify count, then delete original). CSV/temporary exports go to FileManager.temporaryDirectory/exports and never into Documents. Trips, extremes reset times and Preferences live in UserDefaults (already covered by the CA92.1 privacy reason). Sessions list loads manifests only; samples are read on demand and decimated before reaching any Chart.
WHAT CHANGES IN THE SHARED TYPES (all landed in foundation, then owned by WS-A). Reading: adds `monotonic: TimeInterval` (default 0). SessionStats: avgPower becomes time-weighted energyWh*3600/durationS when durationS > 0 (sample mean fallback), adds gapCount/gapSeconds, add(_:) uses monotonic dt when both readings carry it, else timestamp dt. Session: adds schemaVersion, markers, tags, notes, autoStopReason, sampleCount; all decoded with decodeIfPresent so v1 JSON loads; readings stays as the in-memory payload for a fully loaded session. SessionRecorder: gains journal, markers, autoStop, addMarker(label:), checkpoint(). SessionStore: API is summaries-first (see foundation); save/delete/rename/update(notes:tags:)/session(for:)/samples(for:)/csvURL(temp)/recoverInterrupted(). MeterManager: adds trips, extremes, chart, observers, event counters, ReconnectPolicy-driven states, restore identifier, startRecording(name:tags:notes:autoStop:), stopRecording(discard:reason:), addMarker, forgetLastDevice, autoConnectOnLaunch. ConnectionState: adds .reconnecting(name:attempt:nextRetry:) and .unreachable(String), plus shortLabel/symbolName/isTransient/tintToken.

## Foundation (lands in main BEFORE streams start)

Land as ONE commit on main before any worktree branches; then these files are frozen except for their owning stream. Everything below compiles, passes the existing tests, and the app still runs with the old UI.

1. Folder moves (no behaviour change): Views/LiveView.swift stays; Views/HistoryView.swift stays (WS-C replaces); Views/DeviceListView.swift -> Views/Connect/; Views/DiagnosticsView.swift -> Views/Settings/; create empty dirs Views/Live, Views/Sessions, Views/Alerts, Views/Components, Model/Pipeline, Model/Storage, Model/Analysis, Model/Format, Export, Alerts; tests split into WattBenchTests/Core/ProtocolTests.swift, Core/SessionStatsTests.swift, Core/SessionStoreTests.swift (moved verbatim) plus empty Live/, Sessions/, Format/, Alerts/ folders (xcodegen picks up folders).

2. Model/Reading.swift
struct Reading: Codable, Identifiable, Equatable { var id: Date { timestamp }; let timestamp: Date; let voltage: Double; let current: Double; let power: Double; let monotonic: TimeInterval; init(timestamp: Date, voltage: Double, current: Double, power: Double, monotonic: TimeInterval = 0) }  // Codable ignores monotonic (encode nothing, decodeIfPresent -> 0)
struct SessionStats: Codable, Equatable { var samples = 0; var minVoltage, maxVoltage, minCurrent, maxCurrent: Double?; var maxPower: Double = 0; var avgVoltage: Double = 0; var avgCurrent: Double = 0; var meanPowerSampled: Double = 0; var energyWh: Double = 0; var capacityAh: Double = 0; var durationS: Double = 0; var gapCount = 0; var gapSeconds: Double = 0; var avgPower: Double { durationS > 0 ? energyWh * 3600 / durationS : meanPowerSampled }; static let maxGapS: TimeInterval = 5; mutating func add(_ r: Reading); mutating func add(_ r: Reading, dt: TimeInterval) }  // add(_:) computes dt = (r.monotonic > 0 && last.monotonic > 0) ? r.monotonic - last.monotonic : r.timestamp - last.timestamp; dt > maxGapS -> gapCount += 1, gapSeconds += dt, not integrated. Custom decoder: meanPowerSampled decodeIfPresent ?? legacy "avgPower" key.
struct Marker: Codable, Identifiable, Equatable { var id: UUID = UUID(); var timestamp: Date; var label: String; var kind: Kind = .user; enum Kind: String, Codable { case user, gap, autoStop, alert } }
struct Session: Codable, Identifiable, Equatable { static let currentSchema = 2; var schemaVersion: Int = 2; var id: UUID; var name: String; var startTime: Date; var endTime: Date; var deviceName: String?; var stats: SessionStats; var readings: [Reading]; var markers: [Marker] = []; var tags: [String] = []; var notes: String? = nil; var autoStopReason: String? = nil; var isDemo: Bool = false; var duration: TimeInterval; func csv() -> String  /* existing 4 columns first, then elapsed_s, marker_label */ ; func summary() -> SessionSummary }  // init(from:) uses decodeIfPresent for every new field so 1.0 JSON decodes.

3. Model/Storage/SessionSummary.swift
struct SessionSummary: Codable, Identifiable, Equatable { enum State: String, Codable { case recording, complete, recovered }; var schemaVersion: Int = 2; var id: UUID; var name: String; var startTime: Date; var endTime: Date; var deviceName: String?; var stats: SessionStats; var sampleCount: Int; var markers: [Marker]; var tags: [String]; var notes: String?; var autoStopReason: String?; var isDemo: Bool; var state: State; var sparkline: [Float]; var duration: TimeInterval }

4. Model/Storage/SessionStore.swift (foundation implementation = current JSON files, summaries derived at load; WS-A swaps internals)
@MainActor @Observable final class SessionStore { private(set) var summaries: [SessionSummary]; private(set) var loadError: String?; private(set) var saveCount = 0; private(set) var interrupted: SessionSummary?; init(directory: URL? = nil); func load(); func session(for id: UUID) async throws -> Session; func samples(for id: UUID) async throws -> [Reading]; func save(_ s: Session) throws; func delete(id: UUID); func rename(id: UUID, to name: String) throws; func update(id: UUID, notes: String?, tags: [String]?) throws; func csvURL(for s: Session) throws -> URL; func keepInterrupted() throws; func discardInterrupted(); enum StoreError: LocalizedError { case notFound, corruptSamples, io(String) } }

5. Model/Pipeline
struct RingBuffer<Element> { init(capacity: Int); var count: Int; var last: Element?; mutating func append(_ e: Element); func array() -> [Element]; subscript(i: Int) -> Element; mutating func removeAll() }
struct ChartSnapshot: Equatable { var points: [Reading]  /* windowed, <= 600, time ordered */; var publishedAt: Date; var gaps: [DateInterval]; static let empty = ChartSnapshot(points: [], publishedAt: .distantPast, gaps: []) }
struct TripMeter: Codable, Equatable { var label: String; var startedAt: Date; var stats = SessionStats(); mutating func add(_ r: Reading); mutating func reset(at: Date = Date()); var elapsed: TimeInterval { stats.durationS } }
struct Extremes: Codable, Equatable { struct Sample: Codable, Equatable { var value: Double; var at: Date }; var maxV, minV, maxI, minI, maxW: Sample?; var since: Date; mutating func update(_ r: Reading); mutating func reset() }
struct AutoStopRule: Codable, Equatable { var belowCurrentA: Double? ; var forSeconds: TimeInterval = 60; var maxDuration: TimeInterval?; var maxEnergyWh: Double?; enum Reason: String, Codable { case currentBelowThreshold, duration, energy }; private var belowSince: TimeInterval = 0; mutating func evaluate(_ r: Reading, dt: TimeInterval, stats: SessionStats) -> Reason?  /* belowSince accumulates real sample dt only when dt <= SessionStats.maxGapS; resets when current >= threshold * 1.02 */ }
protocol SampleObserver: AnyObject { @MainActor func observe(_ r: Reading, context: SampleContext) }
struct SampleContext { let dt: TimeInterval; let isRecording: Bool; let recordingStats: SessionStats?; let connection: ConnectionState }
struct ReconnectPolicy: Equatable { static let delays: [TimeInterval] = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30]; static let giveUpAfter: TimeInterval = 120; var attempt = 0; var firstFailureAt: Date?; mutating func nextDelay(now: Date) -> TimeInterval?  /* nil = give up */; mutating func reset() }

6. Bluetooth/MeterSource.swift + MeterManager additions (implemented, not stubbed)
protocol MeterSource: AnyObject { var onReading: ((Reading) -> Void)? { get set }; func start(); func stop() }
enum ConnectionState: Equatable { case bluetoothOff, unauthorized, idle, scanning, connecting(String), connected(String), reconnecting(name: String, attempt: Int, nextRetry: Date), unreachable(String), demo; var isConnected: Bool; var isTransient: Bool; var label: String; var shortLabel: String; var symbolName: String; var tintToken: String  /* "green","orange","gray","purple","red" mapped to Color in WS-D */ }
MeterManager gains (with working minimal bodies): private(set) var chart = ChartSnapshot.empty; private(set) var trips: [TripMeter] (1 trip, persisted); private(set) var extremes = Extremes(since: Date()); private(set) var connectionEventCount = 0, recordingEventCount = 0, errorEventCount = 0; private var observers: [any SampleObserver] = []; func addObserver(_:); func startRecording(name: String, tags: [String] = [], notes: String? = nil, autoStop: AutoStopRule? = nil); @discardableResult func stopRecording(discard: Bool = false, reason: String? = nil) -> Session?; func addMarker(label: String); func resetTrip(_ index: Int); func resetExtremes(); func forgetLastDevice(); func retryNow(); var autoConnectOnLaunch: Bool. Old startRecording(name:) removed (LiveView call updated). ingest(_:) is internal (not fileprivate) and calls a pure `SamplePipeline` so tests can drive it: @MainActor final class SamplePipeline { var history: RingBuffer<Reading>; var latest: Reading?; var trips: [TripMeter]; var extremes: Extremes; func ingest(_ r: Reading, recording: SessionRecorder?, observers: [any SampleObserver], connection: ConnectionState) -> ChartSnapshot? }.
SessionRecorder gains: private(set) var markers: [Marker]; var autoStop: AutoStopRule?; let tags: [String]; let notes: String?; func addMarker(label: String, kind: Marker.Kind = .user); func add(_ r: Reading) -> AutoStopRule.Reason?; var journal: RecordingJournal? (nil in foundation).
Model/Storage/RecordingJournal.swift: final class RecordingJournal { static let headerSize = 16, recordSize = 16; init(url: URL, startEpoch: Date, flushInterval: TimeInterval = 1, flushEvery: Int = 64) throws; func append(_ r: Reading); func flush(); func close(); static func read(url: URL) throws -> (start: Date, readings: [Reading]); static func count(url: URL) -> Int }  // foundation ships the type with the format constants and read/append implemented on the main thread; WS-A adds the queue, checkpointing and wiring.

7. Model/Format
enum Metric: String, CaseIterable, Codable, Identifiable { case voltage, current, power; var id: String; var title: String; var symbol: String  /* "V","A","W" */; var colorName: String  /* asset name */; var spokenName: String; func value(_ r: Reading) -> Double }
struct FormattedValue: Equatable { let number: String; let unit: String; var text: String { number + " " + unit } }
struct MetricFormatter { var locale: Locale = .autoupdatingCurrent; var precision: Int = 3  /* significant digits per Preferences */; var autoRange = true; func format(_ v: Double?, _ m: Metric) -> FormattedValue; func energy(_ wh: Double) -> FormattedValue; func capacity(_ ah: Double) -> FormattedValue; func duration(_ s: TimeInterval) -> String; func spoken(_ v: Double?, _ m: Metric) -> String; mutating func formatLive(_ v: Double, _ m: Metric) -> FormattedValue  /* hysteresis: to milli below 0.95, back above 1.05 */ }
enum Fmt { /* kept, each function forwards to MetricFormatter(); marked @available(*, deprecated) */ }
@MainActor @Observable final class Preferences { static let shared: Preferences; var keepAwake: Bool; var heroMetric: Metric; var defaultWindow: Double; var precision: Int; var autoRangeUnits: Bool; var hapticsEnabled: Bool; var showAllDevices: Bool; var autoConnect: Bool; var defaultAutoStop: AutoStopRule?; var alertRulesData: Data?  /* each didSet writes UserDefaults.standard; init(defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) for tests */ }
@MainActor @Observable final class AppRouter { enum Tab: Hashable { case live, sessions }; var tab: Tab = .live; var sessionPath: [UUID] = [] }

### WS-D Settings, Connect, formatting, feedback, app shell

- owns: ios/WattBench/Views/ContentView.swift, ios/WattBench/Views/Connect/DeviceListView.swift, ios/WattBench/Views/Connect/ConnectEmptyState.swift, ios/WattBench/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift, ios/WattBench/Views/Settings/AboutView.swift, ios/WattBench/Views/Settings/DiagnosticsView.swift, ios/WattBench/Views/Components/FeedbackModifiers.swift, ios/WattBench/Views/Components/MetricStyle.swift, ios/WattBench/Views/Components/FloatingChrome.swift, ios/WattBench/Model/Format/Metric.swift, ios/WattBench/Model/Format/MetricFormatter.swift, ios/WattBench/Model/Format/Preferences.swift, ios/WattBench/Model/Format/AppRouter.swift, ios/WattBench/Model/Format/SignalLevel.swift, ios/WattBench/Assets.xcassets/*, ios/WattBenchTests/Format/*.swift

Metric/MetricFormatter/Preferences/AppRouter exactly as in foundation. FeedbackModifiers: `extension View { func connectionFeedback(_ m: MeterManager) -> some View; func recordingFeedback(_ m: MeterManager) -> some View; func saveFeedback(_ s: SessionStore) -> some View; func floatingChrome(_ shape: some InsettableShape) -> some View }`. ### WS-E Alerts, auto-stop rules, notifications

- owns: ios/WattBench/Model/Analysis/ThresholdMonitor.swift, ios/WattBench/Model/Pipeline/AutoStopRule.swift, ios/WattBench/Alerts/AlertCoordinator.swift, ios/WattBench/Alerts/AlertNotifier.swift, ios/WattBench/Alerts/AlertPresets.swift, ios/WattBench/Views/Alerts/AlertsSettingsView.swift, ios/WattBench/Views/Alerts/AlertRuleEditor.swift, ios/WattBench/Views/Components/AlertBanner.swift, ios/WattBenchTests/Alerts/*.swift
- depends on: foundation
- shared contract:

`protocol SampleObserver: AnyObject { @MainActor func observe(_ r: Reading, context: SampleContext) }` and `struct SampleContext { let dt: TimeInterval; let isRecording: Bool; let recordingStats: SessionStats?; let connection: ConnectionState }` (foundation). `@MainActor @Observable final class AlertCoordinator: SampleObserver { var rules: [AlertRule]; private(set) var active: [AlertEvent]; private(set) var alertEventCount: Int; func dismiss(_ id: UUID); func setEnabled(_ id: UUID, _ on: Bool) async }`. `struct AutoStopRule: Codable, Equatable` as in foundation. `struct AlertBanner: View` (reads AlertCoordinator from environment) placed by WS-B via .safeAreaInset(edge: .top). `AlertsSettingsView()` linked from WS-D's SettingsView.

## Tier 1 index

- `A1-crash-safe-background-recording` — Crash-safe recording that survives lock screen, backgrounding and BLE drops [L] → WS-A Core: BLE, pipeline, journal, storage
- `A2-sessions-that-scale` — Summary index + lazy binary samples with migration of 1.0 JSON sessions [M] → WS-A Core: BLE, pipeline, journal, storage
- `A3-sample-pipeline-trips-extremes` — SamplePipeline: ring buffer, 5 Hz chart snapshots, trip meter, peak hold, testability seam [M] → WS-A Core: BLE, pipeline, journal, storage
- `A4-reconnect-policy-autoconnect` — ReconnectPolicy with backoff and give-up, zero-tap auto-connect, event counters [S] → WS-A Core: BLE, pipeline, journal, storage
- `B1-hero-readout-status-pill` — Hero numeral with numericText, tap-to-promote secondary tiles, peak captions, status pill and title menu [M] → WS-B Live instrument face
- `B2-single-scrubbable-chart` — One interactive chart card: V / A / W / All segmented, scrollable window, scrub cursor, peak line, gap bands, markers [L] → WS-B Live instrument face
- `B3-record-bar-setup-sheet-markers` — Bottom Record bar, recording setup sheet with tags/notes/auto-stop, Mark button, save toast with Undo and Discard [M] → WS-B Live instrument face
- `B4-trip-card` — Always-on Trip card under the hero [S] → WS-B Live instrument face
- `C1-session-detail-report` — Session detail as a report: stat tiles, per-metric scroll/zoom chart with envelope, scrub and range selection, markers, rename, notes [L] → WS-C Sessions list, detail, export
- `C2-sessions-list-and-sharelink` — Sessions list with day grouping, search, sort, sparklines, swipe/context actions, and ShareLink + Transferable export [M] → WS-C Sessions list, detail, export
- `D1-formatter-preferences-settings` — MetricFormatter with SI auto-ranging and hysteresis, semantic colour system, Preferences, Settings screen absorbing Diagnostics/demo/keep-awake, feedback modifiers [M] → WS-D Settings, Connect, formatting, feedback, app shell
- `D2-connect-flow` — Connect sheet with actionable empty states, system signal glyph, auto-connect when one meter is found, Advanced disclosure [S] → WS-D Settings, Connect, formatting, feedback, app shell
- `E1-alerts-and-autostop` — Threshold alerts with hysteresis and cooldown, presets, foreground banner + haptic, background local notifications, and the AutoStopRule engine [M] → WS-E Alerts, auto-stop rules, notifications

## Tier 2 (next)

- **Live Activity + Dynamic Island with LiveActivityIntent Stop** — New WattBenchWidgets app-extension target in project.yml, NSSupportsLiveActivities, shared RecordingAttributes in a Shared/ folder, updates throttled to 5 s from MeterManager, layout identical to RecordBar (elapsed, W, Wh, Stop). Ships after A1 has run on the real meter for a week.
- **Automatic event detection with inferred voltage tier** — Pure EventDetector (plug-in/unplug at 20 mA with 1 s debounce, load step max(0.2 A, 25 percent), voltage plateau 5/9/12/15/20/28 V stable 2 s labelled 'inferred', charge complete, gap) replayable over stored sessions; PDO-usage table of time/Wh per level; never names QC/AFC/PPS.
- **Charge-curve phases (Bulk/Taper/Trickle) and hedged time-to-done, Beta** — 20 s smoothed phase segmentation split on gaps, per-phase Wh/avg W bands on the detail chart, one-line summary; ETA only after 2 min of taper with R2 > 0.9 as secondary text; returns 'no charge profile' for resistive and burst loads.
- **Seeded synthetic signal generator for tests and demo scenarios** — xorshift-seeded charge curve, load steps, negotiation steps, power-bank drain, gaps; replaces the two-sine DemoSource with a scenario picker and feeds every analyzer test.
- **Landscape Bench Mode** — Add landscape orientations; on compact vertical size class show ScopeView: full-width MetricChartCard, right column of three large readouts, black background, tab bar hidden, keep-awake; reuses B1/B2 components.
- **Session metadata: device / charger / cable fields with recent-value menus, tag filters** — SessionSummary.meta with three fields and suggestions built from summaries; recording sheet gains the fields; list gets token filters; prerequisite for compare.
- **Session compare overlay (2-4 sessions)** — Multi-select Compare; resample decimated series onto a common elapsed axis aligned on start or first current above threshold; delta table; fixed 4-colour palette distinct from V/A/W.
- **TipKit tips for connect, record, scrub and markers** — Three or four tips donated from views, Reset tips in Settings, no carousel.
- **Dynamic Type and VoiceOver audit** — AXChartDescriptor on both charts, announcements on connect/record, ViewThatFits sweep at AX5, Increase Contrast line widths.
- **Streaming RMS/stddev/peak-to-peak and trapezoid integration in SessionStats** — Welford variance for V/I/P, pk-pk, trapezoid Wh/Ah, merge(other:) for segment stats; public fields preserved.
- **Capacity at nominal cell voltage and delivered-vs-rated for power banks** — mAh @ 3.7 V (selectable 3.6-3.85) rows in Energy sections and the recording card; rated mAh from metadata gives delivered percent.
- **Precision long-window average** — 1/5/15 min Welford mean ± stddev as a hero readout context-menu mode with the ±0.5 percent meter-spec footnote.

## Tier 3 (later)

- **PDF report and JSON export compatible with the desktop app** — ImageRenderer into UIGraphicsPDFRenderer with tiles, chart, markers, phases; wattbench.session.v2 JSON and importer for desktop sessions.
- **App Intents and Siri Shortcuts** — Start/Stop Recording, Connect, Get Reading, Export with AppShortcutsProvider; Stop intent shared with the Live Activity.
- **Home Screen, Lock Screen and StandBy widgets** — Last-session and meter-state widgets via an App Group snapshot once the widget extension exists.
- **Duty-cycle / burst profiler** — Two-centroid split of current over a selected range for TX/RX and sleep/wake loads, surfaced as an Insights row with the 200 ms minimum-burst caveat.
- **Path-resistance estimate from load steps** — Least-squares dV/dI across detected load steps, labelled 'path impedance (estimate)' with a 0.5 A span minimum and no good/poor verdict.
- **.wattbench document type and Files import** — UTExportedTypeDeclarations for the session folder as a package; AirDrop between phones; no iCloud sync.
- **iPad and Designed-for-iPad Mac layout** — TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY 1,2 with NavigationSplitView; all 1.1 components are built size-class aware to make this configuration.
- **Dual-meter efficiency** — Second peripheral slot with paired sessions to compute real input/output efficiency; the one measurement the desktop app faked.
- **Firmware-frame field explorer in Diagnostics** — Live hex diff of the 63-byte frame with candidate Int16/Int32 decodes to discover D+/D-, temperature or the meter's own counters; save raw frames as test fixtures.
- **Localization and String Catalog** — Move all copy into a String Catalog before App Store screenshots; MetricFormatter is already locale-aware.

## Dropped

- FFT / spectrum / oscilloscope views: 10 Hz sampling gives a 5 Hz Nyquist limit; they would be decorative lies.
- Charging-protocol naming (QC 2/3, AFC, Apple 2.4 A, PPS vs QC3 step analysis): needs D+/D- or PD messages the BLE stream does not carry; only an 'inferred voltage tier' survives, in tier 2.
- Temperature readouts and alerts: not in the BLE frame.
- Cable resistance in mOhm with good/ok/poor rating bands: the meter sees charger regulation plus cable plus connectors; a labelled path-impedance estimate is tier 3 instead.
- Desktop-style placeholder efficiency percent: single meter cannot measure it; dual-meter is tier 3.
- iCloud Drive sync, accounts, analytics: the no-network story is a selling point and an App Review simplifier.
- Core Spotlight and Handoff: in-app search covers discovery and there is no second platform yet.
- StoreKit tip jar and alternate icons: adds the Paid Apps agreement and IAP review surface before first submission.
- Apple Watch companion: XL effort, third target, and iPad is sequenced first; Live Activity gives the glance value.
- Circular power/current headroom gauges: a third visual vocabulary on a face that should have one hero number and one chart.
- A separate Bench tab of tool cards and a third Settings tab: the pile-of-toggles failure mode; tools arrive as Insights rows or context-menu modes.
- Photos attached to sessions: camera permission string and storage growth for a marginal gain.
- P-squared streaming percentiles: over-engineering for a 10 Hz stream; exact percentiles can be computed from the file on demand.
- Electricity cost per session: fluff for a bench utility.
- Any third-party charting or BLE dependency: Swift Charts and CoreBluetooth already do the job.
- 1 s / 10 s LOD pyramid files: min/max bucket decimation over the mapped samples is enough below a few hours; revisit if 8-hour sessions become common.

## Risks

- Migration is the one way to lose user data: LegacyMigration must verify counts before deleting a legacy file, keep unreadable files listed, and ship with a v1 fixture test; do a manual migration run on the user's phone (which already holds real sessions) before merging A2.
- Background BLE and App Review: AppStore/metadata.md currently says the app uses Bluetooth only in the foreground; the review note, description and a Battery footnote must be rewritten with A1, and reviewers may ask for a demo video since they have no meter.
- State restoration and journal recovery interact: a relaunch triggered by CoreBluetooth restoration must not both seal the interrupted recording and start a new one; A1 defines 'never auto-resume' and needs on-device testing (BLE is unavailable in the simulator; FixtureSource covers logic only).
- Swift Charts performance with chartScrollableAxes, selection and 600 points at 5 Hz is unproven on older phones; B2 must measure body evaluations with Instruments and fall back to a fixed-window chart with a manual pan if scrolling axes stutter.
- Timestamp jitter: BLE notifications can arrive coalesced (dt 0 then 200 ms); monotonic dt integration is correct on average but chart x spacing shows combs; if visible, smooth display timestamps in ChartSnapshot without touching integration.
- Shared-file conflicts: the foundation commit touches MeterManager, Reading, SessionRecorder/Store and LiveView; streams must branch only after it lands and WS-B must delete the old LiveView sections in one PR so the build never breaks mid-stream.
- Xcode 27 / iOS 26+ SDK changes the look of system controls (Liquid Glass) while the deployment target stays 17; custom chrome must go through FloatingChrome so it can adopt glassEffect, and screenshots must be retaken after the redesign.
- Strict concurrency: annotating MeterManager and friends @MainActor with SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY targeted may surface warnings in CoreBluetooth delegate methods; keep the central on the main queue and mark delegate extensions @MainActor via assumeIsolated where needed.
- Notification permission timing and Focus modes: alerts are only as reliable as the user's notification settings; the Alerts screen must show the current authorization state and the disconnected rule must not spam during a normal reconnect.
- Negative current and flow direction are displayed but not specially integrated (capacityAh can go negative on a power bank being charged); document it in the detail Integrity row and decide signed vs absolute integration before the compare feature.
- Test destination drift: scripts reference iPhone 17 Pro Max; the simulator list on this Mac has it, but CI or another machine may not; parameterise the destination in release.sh.
- Journal flush on a utility queue plus atomic manifest rewrites every 10 s add I/O during long recordings; measure battery over a 4-hour recording and lower the manifest cadence if needed.

## Critic

**Verdict:** The plan is well-shaped and fits the codebase (folder moves, foundation-first, @MainActor, journal, decimation) but it is not safe to fan out to five engineers yet. Four things would break compilation or correctness across streams: (1) nobody owns the "who saves a stopped recording" path, so auto-stop and the notification "Stop & save" action have no way to reach SessionStore; (2) DiagnosticsView (WS-D) still uses ShareSheet defined in HistoryView.swift (WS-C deletes it) and ContentView (WS-D) references HistoryView (WS-C typealiases then deletes it); (3) ChartSnapshot.points is [Reading] but the only decimator returns per-metric DecimatedPoint, and MetricFormatter.formatLive is `mutating` on a struct that SwiftUI bodies cannot mutate; (4) the checked-in project.pbxproj plus five branches adding files guarantees merge conflicts. Two design flaws need fixing before A1/A4 start: reconnect backoff via Task.sleep does not run while the app is suspended (CoreBluetooth pending connects are the real background mechanism), and the journal keys records on wall-clock t_ms while stats use monotonic time, so an NTP jump corrupts the file. App Review items are mostly right, but `.timeSensitive` does require an entitlement, PRIVACY.md still promises foreground-only Bluetooth, and Info.plist has a literal 1.0 so bumping MARKETING_VERSION alone does nothing. With the amendments below, the workstreams can proceed in parallel.

### Missing

- **[blocker] A1/B3/E1 save ownership**: MeterManager has no reference to SessionStore (see WattBenchApp.swift: both created independently; LiveView.stopAndSave does store.save today). The architecture says 'auto-stop -> MeterManager.stopRecording(reason:) -> SessionStore.save' and E1 says the notification 'Stop & save' action calls meter.stopRecording, but neither path can save, and B3 has the view saving on manual stop. Three different owners, one of them nonexistent; a background auto-stop would silently drop the session (well, leave it as an 'interrupted' manifest). → Foundation adds `var onRecordingStopped: ((Session, AutoStopRule.Reason?) -> Void)?` to MeterManager and WattBenchApp.init wires it to `store.save` + counters. ALL stops (manual, auto, notification action, discard=false) go through MeterManager.stopRecording which invokes the hook; RecordBar only calls meter.stopRecording() and reads store.saveCount for the toast. Remove 'saves via store.save' from B3.
- **[blocker] A4 reconnect design**: Backoff implemented as `Task.sleep -> central.connect` only works in the foreground. With bluetooth-central the app is suspended between BLE events, so a 30 s sleep never fires while the screen is off; acceptance 'powering it back on inside the window reconnects without user action' fails on a locked phone. Also cancelling the pending connect at 120 s means a bench meter power-cycled at minute 3 never comes back while the phone is in a pocket. → On unexpected disconnect issue central.connect(peripheral) immediately and leave it pending (CoreBluetooth completes it whenever the peripheral reappears, in background too). ReconnectPolicy drives only the displayed state: .reconnecting(name, since:) then .unreachable after 120 s while the connect stays pending; never cancel while recording. retryNow() re-issues connect. Drop `nextRetry` countdown from ConnectionState (or keep it purely cosmetic). Keep the 1.5 s auto-select in D2.
- **[blocker] A1 journal time base**: Records store UInt32 t_ms from wall-clock startEpoch while stats use monotonic dt. An NTP/timezone correction mid-recording makes t_ms go backwards or negative (UInt32 wrap), breaking ordering, dedupe and replay. Also Reading.id = timestamp already collides on coalesced notifications (dt 0), producing duplicate ForEach IDs in Charts. → t_ms = monotonic seconds since the recording's monotonic start; header stores both startEpoch (wall) and nothing else needed. On read, timestamp = startEpoch + t_ms/1000 and monotonic = t_ms/1000. Change Reading.id to the monotonic value (or an index) and add RecordingJournalTests.testMonotonicOffsetsSurviveWallClockJump.
- **[blocker] Foundation contracts**: Several APIs used across streams are not in the foundation list: MeterManager.clearHistory (B2), meter.devices/hasLastDevice (D2), Preferences.excludeDemoFromTrips (A3/B4), Preferences.capacityUnit and showPeakLine (B2/D1), DeviceListView() and SettingsView() zero-arg inits (B1), RecordingStatusChip() (C2), SampleObserver.swift file not owned by any stream, RecordingStatusChip.swift missing from WS-B owns_files. → Add each to the foundation section and to the owning stream's owns_files; add a one-line 'View inits frozen: DeviceListView(), SettingsView(), AlertsSettingsView(), AlertBanner(), RecordingStatusChip(), RecoverySheet(summary:)' rule.
- **[blocker] ChartSnapshot / Decimator contract**: ChartSnapshot.points is [Reading] 'capped to <= 600 by minMax buckets', but Decimator.minMaxBuckets(metric:) returns [DecimatedPoint] for one metric; the All mode needs V, I and W per point. The two types cannot be reconciled as written and WS-A (pipeline, sparkline) depends on a Decimator owned and modified by WS-C. → Decide now: ChartSnapshot keeps raw Readings (<= 1200 in the 120 s window; that is already <= 600 for windows <= 60 s and 1200 at 2 min, which Swift Charts handles), and Decimator is used only in Sessions detail and for sparklines. Mark Decimator API frozen in foundation (WS-C may add functions, not change signatures). Add `Decimator.meanPower(_:targetCount:) -> [Float]` for the sparkline so WS-A never calls minMaxBuckets.
- **[major] MetricFormatter.formatLive**: `mutating func formatLive` on a struct cannot be called from a SwiftUI body, and the hysteresis state must persist between 10 Hz renders. As specified WS-B cannot compile the hero. → Make the unit-range decision pure: `static func range(for v: Double, metric: Metric, previous: UnitRange?) -> UnitRange` and keep `previous` in HeroReadout @State (or provide `@Observable final class LiveUnitRanger`). MetricFormatter stays a pure struct.
- **[major] Build system / merging**: ios/WattBench.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj is tracked in git while every stream adds 5–15 files; five branches will conflict on it at every merge, and a stale pbxproj compiles the wrong file set. → Foundation commit untracks *.xcodeproj (keep xcshareddata scheme if desired via xcodegen schemes) and adds it to .gitignore; release.sh/run-on-phone.sh already run `xcodegen generate`. Add a CLAUDE.md line: never edit the pbxproj.
- **[major] App Review / entitlements**: E1 says `interruptionLevel .timeSensitive` with 'no entitlements'. Time Sensitive notifications require the com.apple.developer.usernotifications.time-sensitive entitlement (Xcode capability); without it the level is ignored. Also UIBackgroundModes must be paired with a review note and the PRIVACY.md text 'The app never scans in the background' / metadata 'uses Bluetooth only in the foreground' both become false; PRIVACY.md is in no files_to_modify. NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription should mention background use. → Either add an entitlements file via project.yml (`entitlements: path: WattBench/WattBench.entitlements, properties: {com.apple.developer.usernotifications.time-sensitive: true}`) or use `.active`. Add PRIVACY.md and the usage string to A1 files_to_modify with wording: 'stays connected in the background only while you are connected to a meter; never scans in the background; local notifications only, no push'.
- **[major] Info.plist versioning**: WattBench/Info.plist has literal CFBundleShortVersionString 1.0 and CFBundleVersion 1 (xcodegen wrote literals); bumping MARKETING_VERSION in project.yml will not change the shipped version. → In project.yml info.properties set `CFBundleShortVersionString: $(MARKETING_VERSION)` and `CFBundleVersion: $(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`; verify with `plutil -p` on the built app in release.sh.
- **[major] Notifications for unattended runs**: Auto-stop, recovery-after-kill and 'reconnect gave up while recording' produce no notification unless the user happened to enable an alert rule. The whole point of A1+B3 is unattended runs. → E1 owns a `RecordingNotices` path: 'Recording finished · 27.4 Wh (stopped: current below 0.10 A)', 'Meter unreachable, recording paused' (only while recording), 'Recording was interrupted' (posted from the restoration relaunch). Request notification permission when the user first enables auto-stop OR an alert rule (B3 sheet shows the permission footer). Add to AlertNotifier API: `func notifyRecordingStopped(_ s: SessionSummary, reason:)`.
- **[major] Performance at 10 Hz**: latest, recording.stats, trips[0] and extremes are all @Observable properties mutated at 10 Hz; HeroReadout, RecordBar, TripCard and both SecondaryTiles re-render 10 times a second each with numericText springs (25 ms animation retriggered every 100 ms = permanent rolling). @Observable fires on assignment even when extremes did not change. → Pipeline publishes one `DisplayFrame` struct (latest, tripStats, recordingStats, extremes) at 4–5 Hz alongside ChartSnapshot; only `latest` may stay at 10 Hz if the hero is proven smooth. Assign extremes only when changed. Add SamplePipelineTests.testDisplayFrameThrottled. Recommend the hero itself update at 4–5 Hz (the FNB58's own screen refreshes ~2–4 Hz).
- **[major] Journal flush and file protection**: FileHandle.synchronize every 1 s for hours is an fsync per second (battery, flash wear). Separately, if the Data Protection capability is ever set to Complete, writes fail while the phone is locked, which is exactly acceptance criterion 1. → Write every 1 s / 64 records, synchronize every 10 s and on scenePhase .background, stop, and gap. Create the journal with `.completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication` protection explicitly (FileManager attribute) and assert it in RecordingJournalTests. Change 'at most 1 s lost' to 'at most 10 s lost'.
- **[major] Recovery robustness**: Recorder creates samples.wbj then writes manifest.json; a crash in between leaves a folder with no manifest. UIFileSharingEnabled + LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace means users can also delete or edit either file in the Files app. RecoverySheet is presented by WattBenchApp AND inlined by C2 in the Sessions list (double presentation). → A2: SessionStore.load rebuilds a manifest from a journal header when manifest.json is missing, lists 'Samples unavailable' when samples.wbj is missing, ignores unknown files. Write the manifest before opening the journal. Single presenter: WattBenchApp presents RecoverySheet once; C2 shows only a passive 'Recovered' badge.
- **[minor] Elapsed time inconsistency**: A1 says UI elapsed = stats.durationS (excludes gaps); B3 uses Text(timerInterval: startTime...) which is wall-clock; B4 uses durationS. Two different numbers for the same recording. → Rule: live counters show wall-clock via Text(timerInterval:) (cheap, smooth); every stats/report surface shows durationS with 'active' caption and the wall span as secondary. State this once in ui_direction.
- **[minor] CB restoration test seam**: MeterManagerTests.testWillRestoreStateReattachesDelegate needs a fake CBPeripheral; CBPeripheral cannot be instantiated or subclassed usefully in tests, so this test implies an abstraction layer over CoreBluetooth the plan does not budget. → Extract a pure `RestorePlan.make(peripheralStates: [(id, CBPeripheralState, hasServices)]) -> [Action]` and test that; keep willRestoreState as thin glue verified on device. Note willRestoreState arrives before poweredOn, so defer connect until centralManagerDidUpdateState.
- **[minor] Live chart gestures**: chartXSelection(value:) and chartScrollableAxes on the same chart: horizontal drag scrolls, selection needs touch-and-hold; B2 acceptance 'Dragging shows a hairline' contradicts iOS 17 behaviour. In C1, MagnifyGesture + range selection + scrollable axes compound the conflict; programmatic chartScrollPosition writes at 5 Hz fight the user's scroll. → Spec the gesture explicitly: long-press then drag = scrub; horizontal drag = scroll; pinch = zoom (simultaneousGesture). Pin-to-live via a 'following' flag flipped off when the binding changes by more than one snapshot step. Both charts get a 1-day spike prototype before the rest of the stream (already a risk; make it a gate).
- **[minor] Sparklines in List rows**: A Swift Charts view per row (50+ rows) is expensive on scroll; Charts allocates a renderer per instance. → SessionSparkline draws with Canvas/Path from summary.sparkline (60 floats); no Chart in list rows.
- **[minor] Privacy manifest**: If SessionStore/LegacyMigration read contentModificationDate/creationDate (contentsOfDirectory includingPropertiesForKeys or attributesOfItem) the app must declare NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp (C617.1). Plan mentions only CA92.1. → Either avoid timestamp keys (sort by manifest.startTime) or add the FileTimestamp category to PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy in A2.
- **[minor] Accessibility / Dynamic Type**: Hero uses fixed 56pt; secondary captions in metric colours (orange on light) fail contrast at caption size; tap targets on chart segmented pickers fine but the pill's Retry button is small. → Hero via @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) with minimumScaleFactor; metric colour only on values >= .title2, captions .secondary; Retry as a 44pt Button inside the pill. Pull 'Dynamic Type and VoiceOver audit' basics (AX3 layout check) into tier 1 acceptance for B1/C1.
- **[minor] Apple-utility polish gaps**: Not in plan: iOS 18 dark/tinted app icon variants; Home Screen quick actions (Start recording, Connect to last meter); Settings 'Storage: 42 MB · N sessions' with Delete all; undo for session delete (Apple pattern) vs confirmationDialog; landscape lock stays portrait-only. → Add icon variants and Storage row to D1 (S), quick actions to D1 as UIApplicationShortcutItems in project.yml (S). Keep the rest in tier 2.
- **[minor] Migration acceptance wording**: A2 says migrated stats are 'identical', but avgPower semantics change (time-weighted) so the displayed average will differ from 1.0; demo/fixture readings are not quantised to 1/10000 so round-trip equality tests will fail. → Reword to 'all stored fields identical, sampleCount identical, spacing identical'; fixtures must be pre-quantised (generate with Int32 math).
- **[minor] Ownership of scripts**: release.sh / run-on-phone.sh / .gitignore / CLAUDE.md iOS section are in no owns_files but the plan edits them (destination parameter, pbxproj rule). → Assign to WS-A foundation.

### Conflicts

- DiagnosticsView.swift (WS-D) uses `ShareSheet` defined in HistoryView.swift (WS-C). C1 deletes ShareSheet and the `URL: @retroactive Identifiable` extension; if C1 merges before D1 the target does not compile. Fix: foundation replaces DiagnosticsView's share with `ShareLink(item: meter.diagnosticsText)` and deletes ShareSheet/URL extension there (both trivial), so neither stream touches the other's file.
- ContentView.swift (WS-D) references `HistoryView()`; C2 reduces HistoryView to a typealias 'then deleted at the end'. Fix: WS-D keeps `HistoryView()`; the typealias deletion is a post-merge cleanup commit, not part of WS-C. Same for the `Fmt` shim (lives in ContentView.swift, WS-D): D1 must not delete it; final cleanup commit removes it after grep shows no callers.
- WattBenchApp.swift is WS-A's, but E1 needs wiring there (AlertCoordinator.onAlert -> meter.addMarker, notification action -> stopRecording, UNUserNotificationCenter delegate before launch completes) and B3/E1 need the save hook. Fix: foundation lands `AlertCoordinator.onAlert`, `AlertCoordinator.onStopAndSave`, `MeterManager.onRecordingStopped` closures and assigns them in WattBenchApp; E1 drops the 'AppDelegate adaptor owned by this stream' wording (an @UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor can only be declared in WattBenchApp; setting UNUserNotificationCenter.current().delegate in AlertNotifier.init is enough).
- Decimator.swift is 'landed in foundation', owned by WS-C and listed in C1 files_to_modify, yet WS-A A2 (sparkline) and A3 (ChartSnapshot windowing) call it. Freeze the signatures in foundation; WS-C may only add.
- AutoStopRule.swift is owned by WS-E (E1 modifies) but SessionRecorder.add (WS-A, A1) evaluates it and B3 composes it. Freeze `struct AutoStopRule` fields + `evaluate` signature in foundation; E1 changes bodies and tests only.
- TripCard.swift appears in B4 files_to_add and B3 files_to_modify (same stream, fine) but B3 must land after B4; state the order inside WS-B.
- Preferences.showAllDevices (WS-D) vs MeterManager.showAllDevices didSet restartScan (existing, WS-A) and DeviceListView's `$meter.showAllDevices` binding. Decide: MeterManager keeps the property and persists it; Preferences does not duplicate it.
- SessionExport contract says `struct SessionExport: Transferable { let session: Session }` but C2 spec says it takes a summary and loads samples via store.session(for:) inside the exporting closure (off-main, needs MainActor hop). Pick the summary form: `SessionExport(summary:, loader: @Sendable (UUID) async throws -> Session)` injected from the view.
- StatusPill (WS-B) shows `retry in` from ConnectionState.reconnecting(nextRetry:) and D2's Connect sheet does the same; if A4 adopts pending-connect (recommended) that case changes shape. Settle ConnectionState cases in foundation before branching: .reconnecting(name: String, since: Date) and .unreachable(String).
- Model/Pipeline/SampleObserver.swift (SampleObserver + SampleContext) is created in foundation but owned by nobody; assign to WS-A.

### Tier-1 amendments

- A1: replace 'flush every 1 s with synchronize' by 'write every 1 s or 64 records; synchronize every 10 s, on gap, on scenePhase .background and on stop'; add explicit .completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication file protection; t_ms is monotonic offset from recording start; write manifest before opening journal; add MeterManager.onRecordingStopped hook and route every stop through it; add PRIVACY.md + NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription to files_to_modify; acceptance 'at most 10 s lost'.
- A1: stopRecording should not read 144k samples back just to build a Session; return a Session with `readings: []` plus sampleCount and let the sparkline come from a recorder-maintained 1 Hz mean-power array (Float, 3600/h). Change the SessionStore.save(_:) rule to 'if samples.wbj exists, write manifest only' (already there) and stop claiming 'single pass read-back'.
- A2: add 'rebuild manifest from journal header when manifest.json is missing; tolerate unknown files in Documents/sessions; sort by manifest startTime, no file timestamps (or add FileTimestamp privacy reason)'; reword migration acceptance to 'stored fields identical'; untrack xcodeproj and parameterise release.sh destination in this stream.
- A3: publish a throttled DisplayFrame (latest, trip stats, recording stats, extremes) at 5 Hz next to ChartSnapshot; ChartSnapshot.points stays raw Readings (max 1200), Decimator not used in the live path; assign extremes only when changed; gate the 200 ms timer and readRSSI on scenePhase == .active; add Preferences.excludeDemoFromTrips to foundation.
- A4: rewrite spec around a pending central.connect that is never cancelled while recording; ReconnectPolicy only drives displayed state (.reconnecting(since:) -> .unreachable after 120 s); retryNow re-issues connect; drop nextRetry countdown; keep counters and auto-connect on poweredOn.
- B1: hero font via @ScaledMetric; hero reads DisplayFrame (5 Hz) not latest unless prototype proves 10 Hz numericText looks right; Retry in pill is a 44pt button; captions never in metric colour.
- B2: specify gestures (long-press-drag scrub, drag scroll, pinch none on live); 'following' flag logic for pin-to-live; add a day-1 spike gate that measures body evaluations before building the rest; add meter.clearHistory to the MeterManager contract.
- B3: RecordBar never calls store.save; it calls meter.stopRecording() and reacts to store.saveCount / lastSavedSummary for the toast; permission footer for notifications when auto-stop is enabled; elapsed = Text(timerInterval:) wall clock, stats show durationS.
- C1: SessionExport takes a summary + async loader; RecoverySheet not inlined (badge only); spike MagnifyGesture + range selection + scrollable axes before committing; Sparkline via Canvas not Chart (C2).
- C2: keep `typealias HistoryView = SessionsListView` until a post-merge cleanup; do not delete ShareSheet (foundation already removed it).
- D1: MetricFormatter.formatLive replaced by a pure range function + @State; Fmt shim deletion moved to post-merge cleanup; add Storage row (bytes used, session count, Delete all sessions with confirmation), iOS 18 dark/tinted icon variants, UIApplicationShortcutItems (Start recording, Connect to last meter); fix Info.plist version wiring in project.yml.
- D2: reflect the new ConnectionState shape (.reconnecting(since:)) and keep MeterManager.showAllDevices as the single owner.
- E1: remove 'AppDelegate adaptor owned by this stream'; add entitlements file for time-sensitive or use .active; add RecordingNotices (finished / paused-unreachable / interrupted) with permission requested on first auto-stop or rule; AlertCoordinator gains onAlert/onStopAndSave closures assigned in foundation's WattBenchApp.
- Foundation additions: MeterManager.onRecordingStopped, clearHistory, devices/hasLastDevice frozen; Preferences.excludeDemoFromTrips/capacityUnit/showPeakLine; frozen zero-arg view inits; Decimator + AutoStopRule signatures frozen; SampleObserver.swift and RecordingStatusChip.swift added to owns_files; DiagnosticsView switched to ShareLink and ShareSheet/URL extension deleted; .gitignore xcodeproj; Reading.id off timestamp; CFBundleShortVersionString/CFBundleVersion bound to build settings.
- Add a 'post-merge cleanup' pseudo-workstream (owner: whoever merges last): delete HistoryView typealias, delete Fmt, grep for .blue/.orange/.green literals, retake screenshots, run the migration on the user's phone before A2 ships.
